This matter is taken up through hybrid mode.

2. Petitioner in this writ petition seeks to assail the order dated 4th July, 2024 (Annexure-10) passed by the Collector, Balangir - Opposite Party No.3, rejecting her representation for compensation for structure and water bodies.

3. Ms. Mahapatra, learned counsel for the Petitioner submits that pursuant to Notification No.
40312 dated 28th November, 2022 under Section 11 of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (for brevity 'the Act'),
the land of the Petitioner was acquired.

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: The Collector directed for assessment of structure and water bodies over the property to assess the compensation.
On receiving the report, estimation was made and sent to the Department of Water Resources for sanction.
It is submitted that the Water Resources Department is understood to have accorded sanction to the estimate submitted by the Collector, Balangir - Opposite Party No.3.
In spite of the same, the Petitioner was only awarded compensation for landed property and not for the structure and water bodies.

Hence, she filed a Debaki Patra vs State Of Odisha on 26 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/143824746/
1 representation before the Collector, Balangir to make an assessment of the structure and water bodies and pay the compensation accordingly.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The said objection was not paid any heed, for which the Petitioner approached this Court in W.P.(C) No. 10009 of 2024 which was disposed of on 26th April, 2024 with a direction to the Collector, Balangir to dispose of the representation of the Petitioner.
Pursuant to the said direction order under Annexure-10 has been passed.

It is submitted that the enquiry conducted by the Committee constituted by the Collector, Balangir in absence of the Superintending Engineer who is an expert, was perfunctory as the Committee did not take into consideration the valuation report prepared and submitted by the Superintending Engineer earlier on the basis of which sanction of compensation was made.

Although these facts were brought to the notice of the Collector, Balangir, but without considering the same, the impugned order under Annexure-10 has been passed relying upon the report of the Committee which prepared on the basis of an enquiry which was perfunctory.
Hence, finding no other alternative, this writ petition has been filed.

4. Mr. Dash, learned Additional Standing Counsel vehemently objects to the same and submits that since the Petitioner has an efficacious remedy under Section 64 of the Act to pray for referring the matter to the Authority for redressal of her grievances, a writ petition would not be maintainable.

He, therefore, prays for dismissal of the writ petition.
5.

Taking note of the submission made by learned counsel for the parties, this Court finds that the grievance of the Petitioner is with regard to non-payment of compensation with regard to the structure and water bodies over the land acquired.
Thus, the case of the Petitioner is squarely coming under Section 64 of the Act.
It is however submitted at the bar that the Petitioner has received the compensation for the landed property during 2023.
In the meantime, more than one year has already elapsed.

6. Be that as it may, since the Petitioner is agitating her grievance for compensation with regard to structure and water bodies and pursuing litigation in different forums since the date of receipt of compensation, she should be given an opportunity to file an application under Section 64 of the Act to refer the matter to the Authority.

7. Accordingly, this Court without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case of the Petitioner to get compensation for structure and water bodies, if any, available on the land acquired, disposes of the writ petition with a direction that in the event the Petitioner files an application under Section 64 of the Act within a period of four weeks hence, before the Collector, Bolangir - Opposite Party No.3, he shall without going into technicalities, refer the matter to the Authority for adjudication, as expeditiously as possible, preferably within a period of six weeks from the date of filing of such application.
Urgent certified copy of this order be granted on proper application.
